configuration.note: Bounds, opacity and the data URI are checked in validateWorkflow; the georeference's CORRECTNESS is not checkable here and is recorded as not established in experiment 143.

ports.note: The `ground` port type was added to the closed union for this widget, which is a base-contract change made deliberately under D4. A plate must not reach clip_raster or sample_raster: its pixels are ink, and sampling them returns the colour of a line. The port type makes that connection impossible rather than reporting it after it is made.

ontology.note: GAP, meaning no alignment to an external cartographic vocabulary -- not meaning the terms are undeclared. fw:MapImageInput and fw:MapImage are declared in ontology/runtime.ttl with their properties. The receipt asserts the digest, the pixel dimensions, the four bounds, the ground resolution in metres and `fw:layerRole "context"`, which is the limit stated where a reader meets the layer rather than only in a document.

changes.description: Where to look, in a worked example (experiment 201): an example can name the features to find, in order, each with why it was chosen and where it is on the image and on the map, sized to the feature. In Configure…, the feature to find next and its reason are said, a slow pulse (2.4 s a cycle, still under reduced motion) marks the area on both panes, and each click is told whether it landed on the feature. Nothing is filled for the learner; a setting turns the pulse off. The Inspector says how many features the example names.

evidence.note: Nine unit tests over the world-file reader, the extent it derives, the ground resolution and each refusal: a rotated world file, a flipped image, crossed corners, corners outside the world, and a projection that sends the plate nowhere finite. Checked against the example's own geo/map2.jgw byte for byte. That the georeference is CORRECT. The control points were placed by a reader of the plate and this draws what they recorded; an alignment error looks exactly like a correct placement. Measuring the residual against modern boundaries is what would close it. That a reader understands what a historical wash means. The plate's own legend and the example's prose do that work. That 1002x788 over South London, about 40 m per pixel, is enough for anything but ground. There is nothing here for a lab check to recompute -- placing an image where its georeference says has no second implementation that could disagree -- so widgets/check-coverage.json records `none` with that reason rather than claiming parity this project's arithmetic would be agreeing with itself about. 0.2.0: tests/georeference.test.mjs (4: an exact affine recovered; too few or collinear points refused; South London's four points refitted, north-south agreeing with the hand fit and east-west differing by the direction of the fit; a turned image drawn through a matrix) and tests/map-image.test.mjs. 0.3.0: tests/georeference.test.mjs (5: a click on a guide feature, on each pane, within its radius) and tests/georeference-dialog.browser.mjs (the feature and its reason named, the pulse on both panes at 2.4 s, a click on the feature said, nothing filled, the pulse off on request and still under reduced motion).
